_readme.title: Manufacturer Registration Examples (UI / API aligned)
_readme.description: Adding a manufacturer requires TWO separate steps. Read carefully.

step_1.what: Register the manufacturer as an application USER (PostgreSQL only)
step_1.who: Anyone / the manufacturer themselves, OR an Admin
step_1.effect: Creates a login account in PostgreSQL. Does NOT touch the blockchain.

step_2.what: Whitelist the manufacturer's wallet on the Ethereum Smart Contract
step_2.who: Admin ONLY (requires owner_private_key / OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY env var)
step_2.effect: Calls addManufacturer() on ProductRegistry.sol. Spends gas. Stored on-chain permanently.

payload_shape.name: string  (company display name)
payload_shape.owner_private_key: 0x + 64 hex chars (admin/owner MetaMask private key) OR omit to use OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY env var

important_notes: wallet_address is a PUBLIC 42-char Ethereum address (starts with 0x). It is SAFE to share.
owner_private_key is a SECRET 66-char string (0x + 64 hex). NEVER share it. Keep in .env.
A manufacturer can only register products on-chain AFTER Step 2 completes.
Step 1 (PostgreSQL) gives them a UI login. Step 2 (Blockchain) gives them product-registration rights.
If you omit owner_private_key in Step 2, the service reads OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY from the environment.

step_2_blockchain_whitelist.note: wallet_address here MUST be the same address used in Step 1 for the same manufacturer.

examples._label: Step 2 WITHOUT owner_private_key (uses OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY env var automatically)
examples.name: Xiaomi Technology

ui_form_fields_reference.description: These are the exact fields shown in the UI Add Manufacturer card (Admin tab)

Wallet Address (Public).format: 0x followed by 40 hex characters = 42 chars total

Owner Private Key.format: 0x followed by 64 hex characters = 66 chars total
Owner Private Key.note: This is the Hardhat default test key. NEVER use real private keys in examples.
